questions.problem: Express $5{cos}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘}-5{sin}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘}$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
questions.worked_solution:
Our expression can be factored as follows:

$$
5({cos}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘}-{sin}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘})
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={16}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘}-{sin}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {16}^{∘})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}5({cos}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘}-{sin}^{2}⁡{16}^{∘}) & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡{32}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{4}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12})-2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12}){sin}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12})+{sin}^{4}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12}) & ={({cos}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12}))}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{7\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12}) & =cos\,(2\cdot \frac{7\pi }{12}) \\  & =cos\,(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{({cos}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{12}))}^{2} & ={(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}=\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
